column2: page_alloc: more extensive free page checking with debug_pagealloc

column1: The page allocator checks struct pages for expected state (mapcount
flags etc) as pages are being allocated (check_new_page()) and freed
(free_pages_check()) to provide some defense against errors in page
allocator users.
Prior commits 479f854a207c (""mm
pages allocated from the PCP"") and 4db7548ccbd9 (""mm
debugging checks of freed pages until a PCP drain"") this has happened
for order-0 pages as they were allocated from or freed to the per-cpu
caches (pcplists).  Since those are fast paths
performed only when pages are moved between pcplists and global free
lists.  This however lowers the chances of catching errors soon enough.
In order to increase the chances of the checks to catch errors
kernel has to be rebuilt with CONFIG_DEBUG_VM
multiple other internal debug checks (VM_BUG_ON() etc)
suboptimal when the goal is to catch errors in mm users
itself.
To catch some wrong users of the page allocator we have
CONFIG_DEBUG_PAGEALLOC
column2: which is designed to have virtually no overhead

column1: unless enabled at boot time.  Memory corruptions when writing to freed
pages have often the same underlying errors (use-after-free
as corrupting the corresponding struct pages
functionality is a good fit to extend by also perform struct page checks
at least as often as if CONFIG_DEBUG_VM was enabled.
Specifically
column3: when debug_pagealloc is enabled on boot

column1: and CONFIG_DEBUG_VM disabled
column2: pages are checked when allocated from or

column1: freed to the pcplists *in addition* to being moved between pcplists and
free lists.  When both debug_pagealloc and CONFIG_DEBUG_VM are enabled
pages are checked when being moved between pcplists and free lists *in
addition* to when allocated from or freed to the pcplists.
When debug_pagealloc is not enabled on boot
should be virtually none thanks to the use of static key.
